name: Whales

subjectOf.text: Any blockchain whose soft forks are decided through private communication between famous token holding whales is ultimately less secure than legacy centralized systems, which at least address centralized security risks deliberately.
subjectOf.abstract: Any blockchain subject to such governance is ultimately less secure than legacy centralized systems which pointedly address centralized security risks.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Secure Proof of Stake Protocol (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3125827
scope_conditions: off chain governance conducted privately among large holders and developers

subjectOf.text: If reputation whales stake reputation on a project and the market commits the capital for that stake, the whales should still receive part of the ROI because it is their reputation that is at stake, and they are not required to commit capital or to support capital calls with liquidity.
subjectOf.abstract: If whales stake but the market commits for their stake with capital, whales should still have the right to receive (part of) the ROI because it is their reputation that is at stake. Whales are not required to commit capital and don't have to support capital calls with liquidity.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
scope_conditions: whale reputation that has become meaningful through a track record

subjectOf.text: Small market cap launches at very cheap initial prices carry the potential for team and whale purchase abuses, which is why equitable treatment of the public requires significant project-controlled liquidity.
subjectOf.abstract: Small market cap launches at very cheap initial prices bring with them the potential abuses of team and whale purchases.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908

subjectOf.text: The larger the market capitalization controlled by the DAO, the less likely it becomes that whales and insiders can purchase inexpensive tokens on the market.
subjectOf.abstract: The larger the market capitalization that is controlled by the DAO, the less likely it becomes that whales and insiders can purchase inexpensive tokens on the market.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908

subjectOf.text: Whale purchases that soak up token supply at the earliest possible time in a launch are the key problem fair launch platforms address, because they can be the origin of significant centralization that harms the project for the entirety of its active market engagement.
subjectOf.abstract: of whale token purchases that soak up supply at the earliest possible time in the token launch. Such whale purchases can be the origin of significant centralization of a token launch that may harm the project for the entirely of its active market engagement.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: whales able to buy large amounts at the earliest moment of a launch
